A soaring barrel-vaulted palm nave, its riveted iron ribs arcing up and off both top corners of the frame, slim white-painted glazing ribs fanning between the panes overhead and the wet glazed flank running out past the left edge; a brass spiral stair climbs the near pier to a slatted catwalk that runs the whole length at canopy height, seen obliquely from the edge of the sunken bed, looking up along the ribs.

A tiered glasshouse built like a wedding cake, three round glazed storeys stepping inward, each ring smaller than the one below; the nearest ring of curved panes fills the right third of the frame and its iron ring-beam crosses the top, a bronze stair spiralling up through a hole in each tier, seen from the second tier's walkway looking across and down through the open middle.

A great dome raised over an oak that stood here first, the trunk breaking straight up through the brick floor and the ironwork shaped around it in a ring of shorter ribs; the dome's wet panes fill the upper frame and run off the top-left corner, a plank catwalk circling the trunk at branch height on brass brackets, seen from the floor beside the trunk looking up and along the ring.

A long glasshouse standing out from a cliff on iron stilts, its floor a grating you can see daylight through, the curved glazed roof arcing off the top of the frame and the outer glass wall filling the whole right edge, a short ladder-stair up to a narrow inspection walk under the ridge, seen from the inner end looking along the house with the beds falling away.

A small ornate glasshouse standing complete INSIDE a far larger one, its own little glazed pitched roof and brass finial rising in the middle distance while the great house's ribs and panes arch high above and off both top corners; a stair goes up the big house's flank to a gallery, seen from that gallery half-height, looking down onto the little roof among the palms.

Two houses through one inner glass wall: a hot jungle nave in front, its wet panes filling the upper frame and running off the left edge, and beyond the misted inner glass a cold frost-fern house going pale and blue; an iron stair in the near corner rises to a catwalk that crosses above the dividing wall, seen from beside the connecting door, obliquely.

A long curving lean-to glasshouse laid against an old brick garden wall, the brick warm and trained with fruit down the whole left side, the single-slope glazed roof running up out of the top-right corner with its slim ribs in a shallow fan; a plank step-up and a running board along the wall at waist height, seen from the low end three-quarters along, looking up the curve.

An octagonal glazed pavilion crowned with a brass lantern top, its eight iron corner-posts standing in the beds and the curved panes of two faces filling the left and upper frame, a tight cast-iron stair winding up to a railed ring under the lantern, seen from one corner of the floor looking diagonally across to the far post.

The fan-shaped apse end of a great nave, the ribs radiating from a single high boss like the spokes of an umbrella and running off the top and right of the frame, every pane above beaded with water; an iron gallery crosses the mouth of the apse on slim columns, seen from the side aisle below, oblique, looking up into the fan.

A sunken pit-house whose floor lies a full storey below the garden, so the glazed sides start at knee height and the glass roof sits low and close overhead, crossing the whole top of the frame; brick steps with a brass handrail climb out at the far end, seen from the bottom of the steps looking along the low warm tunnel of beds.

A three-storey glass tower with an open well down the middle, iron galleries ringing the well at each floor and the tall glazed flank filling the right of the frame from floor to ceiling with its ribs cropped by the top edge; a bolted iron stair zigzags up one side, seen from the first gallery looking obliquely across the well and up.

A glasshouse bridging a canal, its arched glazed roof springing from parapet to parapet and arcing off both top corners, a strip of thick glass set into the floor so green water-light comes up through it onto the leaves; a few steps and a landing at one end, seen from the middle of the span looking along it at an angle.

A long low vinery under a ridge-and-furrow roof, the glazed folds running away in a zigzag across the top of the frame and the near fold cropped by the upper-left corner, vine rods trained along wires just under the glass; a rolling plank platform on cast wheels to reach the ridge, seen from beside it, looking down the furrows.

A glasshouse roofed over an abandoned stone quarry, the raw cut rock face making the whole back wall and the iron-and-glass roof spanning the pit from rim to rim, its ribs crossing the upper frame and running off to the right; stone-cut steps and an iron handrail climb the rock to a bolted walkway, seen from the quarry floor looking up the face.

A glasshouse raised over a steaming hot spring, the rock pools breathing white vapour into the roof space, the glazed ribs arcing overhead into haze and running off the top-left corner while the wet glass flank fills the right edge; duckboards and a short brass-railed stair to a viewing deck, seen from the duckboards beside the nearest pool.

A vast single dome with a ring catwalk at half-height and a chain hoist hanging from the central boss, the riveted ribs converging high above and cropped by the top of the frame, condensation running down the curved panes that fill the left edge; the catwalk reached by a spiral stair in the near pier, seen from the floor looking up past the hoist chain.

A conservatory the size of a railway shed, one enormous iron arch after another marching away down the house, the nearest arch cropped at both top corners and the glazed end wall a soft bright haze far off; an iron gantry walk runs along the springing line of the arches, seen from under the second arch, obliquely across the beds.

A glasshouse framed like an upturned boat, its curved iron ribs closing overhead exactly as a hull's would, the ribs running off the top of the frame and the glazed flank off the left; a narrow keel-walk of planks down the centre and a short stair to a stern platform, seen from beside the walk looking up into the ribs.

A glazed crossing where two great naves meet at right angles, four iron piers carrying a raised octagon of glass above, ribs radiating from it across the whole top of the frame and one nave's flank glass filling the right edge; stairs climb two of the piers to a balcony ring, seen from under the crossing looking diagonally down one nave.

A conservatory grafted straight onto the side of a stone house, so its inner wall is the house's own dressed masonry with two lit windows in it, the glazed roof sweeping up from that wall and off the top-right corner, the outer panes filling the lower right; a few stone steps and a landing to the house door, seen from the far corner of the beds, oblique.

A low propagating house, roof close enough overhead to touch, its glazed slope crossing the top of the frame and the near glass wall cropped down the left edge, benches running the length at hip height on iron legs; a single step up to a raised end bench, seen from the aisle between the benches, looking along it at an angle.

A tall glasshouse with a working brass lift in an open iron cage standing right in the middle of the floor, its guide rails going straight up through the roof space to a gallery, the dome's ribs and panes arcing off both top corners behind it; the gallery also reached by a stair, seen from beside the cage looking up and past it.

An amphitheatre glasshouse, the beds stepping down in curved terraces to a pool at the bottom, the glazed roof arching over the whole bowl and cropped at the top of the frame, the flank panes running off the right edge; a curved stair follows the terraces down, seen from three steps up, looking obliquely across the bowl.

A lily house, a shallow warm pool taking nearly the whole floor with only a narrow brick margin round it, the low glazed roof close above the water and crossing the entire top of the frame, its ribs doubled in the reflection; a short stair to a corner platform over the water, seen from the brick margin at the pool's shoulder.

A glasshouse whose end wall is one great curved bay of hundreds of small panes bowing outward, the bay filling the right half of the frame from floor to ribs and the roof's ironwork running off the top-left; a plank gallery crosses the bay at half height on brass brackets, seen from the floor to one side, looking up into the curve.
